summary: @servicetitan/lazy-module preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated 727KB payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is obfuscated (obfuscator.io transform) and, when Bun is not already present on the host, downloads a Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun, extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a single-line ~727KB Bun-compiled CJS bundle with obfuscator.io fingerprints (hex-named identifiers, a rotating string array, and a large numeric constant table). The package's declared purpose is a React Suspense/lazy-module wrapper, which has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime at install time in order to run an opaque bundle. The alternate-runtime step is used to execute code that the standard Node toolchain and static scanners cannot readily inspect; the payload's contents and network destinations are not observable from source. This install-time execution of an obfuscated payload via a bootstrapped alternate runtime is the evasive dropper pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
